about: Hand-checked scholarships for veterans, service members and their families. Each entry was read on the sponsor's own page on the date in 'checked'. 'students' = who may apply (veteran, service_member, spouse, surviving_spouse, child, grandchild); 'situations' = the military member's situation a family member needs (serving, retired, veteran, disabled, fallen) -- empty means any; 'branches' empty means all. Amounts and dates change every year: Jarvet must say to confirm on the sponsor's site. Re-check yearly (scripts/check-counselor.py --links checks the links).

finder.name: CareerOneStop Scholarship Finder (U.S. Department of Labor)
finder.note: More than 9,500 scholarships, fellowships and grants; searchable by keyword, state, level of study and more. A 'veteran' search returned 100 awards on 2026-09-25.

scam_warning.text: Never pay to apply for a scholarship. If a company promises a scholarship or grant in exchange for a processing cost, redemption fee or other upfront payment, walk away. The FAFSA is always free, and never share your FSA ID (the username and password for the FAFSA) with anyone.
scam_warning.source: Federal Trade Commission, How To Avoid Scholarship and Financial Aid Scams

scholarships.name: Tillman Scholars
scholarships.timing: Applications open December 1 each year; the deadline varies (the window can run November to February). The 2026 class is closed.
scholarships.rules: Service members of any branch, veterans of pre- and post-9/11 eras, spouses of active-duty or veteran service members, and surviving spouses. Must be full-time in a bachelor's, master's or professional degree at an accredited U.S. school (can apply before enrolling). No minimum GPA to apply; 3.0 to renew.

scholarships.name: Student Veterans of America partner scholarships
scholarships.amount: $10,000 each (2026: five for mental health counseling students; two for Navy and two for Army student veterans in engineering, operations, logistics, manufacturing or related fields)
scholarships.timing: The 2026 applications were open March 31 to May 1, 2026; new partner scholarships are posted each year.
scholarships.rules: For student veterans; each partner scholarship has its own field and branch rules. SVA says the awards do not interfere with the GI Bill or other financial aid.

scholarships.name: Sport Clips Help A Hero Scholarship
scholarships.sponsor: Veterans of Foreign Wars (VFW) with Sport Clips
scholarships.timing: Awarded twice a year: fall scholarships in August, spring scholarships in January.
scholarships.rules: Retired, honorably discharged, active duty, or National Guard/Reserve, and accepted to or enrolled in a VA-approved program at an accredited school. One award per family per semester; must be used that semester.

scholarships.name: AMVETS National Scholarships
scholarships.amount: Veterans and active duty/Guard/Reserve: two $12,000 awards plus $4,000 awards; spouses/widows, children and grandchildren: $4,000 awards
scholarships.timing: Yearly; see the AMVETS page for this year's dates.
scholarships.rules: For veterans, active duty, Guard and Reserve, their spouses or widows, children and grandchildren. Meant to fill the gap left after federal and state grants and scholarships are used.

scholarships.name: Folds of Honor Higher Education Scholarship
scholarships.amount: Up to $2,500 per term ($1,250 part-time), for unmet need (tuition, fees, required books; housing and meals for higher education)
scholarships.timing: Application window February 1 to March 31 each year.
scholarships.rules: Spouses and dependents of U.S. service members who were killed or disabled (see Folds of Honor for its definition). Pays unmet need after other aid; a 2.0 GPA for the last two terms is required when accepting. School must be accredited (or state-registered for some licensure programs).

scholarships.name: Scholarships for Military Children
scholarships.amount: $2,000 (at least one award at each commissary with eligible applicants)
scholarships.timing: Yearly; see militaryscholar.org for this year's dates.
scholarships.rules: Children of active duty, reserve and retired military members.

scholarships.name: Heroes' Legacy Scholarships
scholarships.timing: Yearly; see the Fisher House page for this year's dates.
scholarships.rules: Children of service members who died or became seriously injured in the line of duty since 9/11. Can be combined with Scholarships for Military Children; supplements other grants (total may not exceed the cost of attendance).

scholarships.name: American Legion Legacy Scholarship
scholarships.amount: Up to $20,000 for children of the fallen; up to $5,000 for children of disabled veterans
scholarships.timing: 2026 deadline was March 25, 2026 (awards announced in May); yearly.
scholarships.rules: Children (including adopted and stepchildren) of service members who died on active duty on or after September 11, 2001, or of post-9/11 veterans with a combined VA disability rating of 50% or more. Needs-based: fills the gap after federal and state aid (including GI Bill or Fry). Can reapply up to six times.

scholarships.name: Mrs. Patty Shinseki Spouse Scholarship
scholarships.timing: Year-round, no deadline; reapply every year.
scholarships.rules: Spouses of Soldiers who are active duty, retired (including medically retired and grey-area retirees), deceased on active duty or in retirement, or AGR/Army Reserve on Title 10 orders all year; listed in DEERS. For a first undergraduate degree or first technical certification.

scholarships.name: Maj. Gen. James Ursano Scholarship for Dependent Children
scholarships.timing: 2026-2027 cycle ran January 1 to April 1, 2026; yearly.
scholarships.rules: Children under 24 of Soldiers who are active duty, retired (including medically retired and grey-area retirees), deceased on active duty or in retirement, or AGR/Army Reserve on Title 10 orders all year; listed in DEERS. For a first undergraduate degree or technical certification; trade schools count.

scholarships.name: Navy-Marine Corps Relief Society Education Assistance
scholarships.amount: Scholarships $500 to $3,000 per year, based on cost of attendance and the FAFSA Student Aid Index; interest-free loans may be available outside the application window
scholarships.timing: Yearly application window (watch their site for the 2027-28 window).
scholarships.rules: Children (under 23 by September 30 of the academic year) and spouses of active-duty, retired or qualifying deceased Sailors and Marines. Needs a FAFSA.

scholarships.name: General Henry H. Arnold Education Grant
scholarships.amount: Varies, based on family financial need
scholarships.timing: Yearly; see the AFAS page for this year's dates.
scholarships.rules: Dependents of Airmen and Guardians; awarded on family financial need. AFAS also offers the "Bee" Arnold Spouse Tuition Program for short job training (3 to 12 weeks) or part-time undergraduate study, and merit scholarships.

scholarships.name: Marine Corps Scholarship Foundation scholarships
scholarships.timing: Degree students: January 1 to March 1 each year. Non-degree certificate programs: year-round.
scholarships.rules: Children or stepchildren of an active-duty, Reserve or veteran Marine (veterans need an honorable discharge), a Marine killed while serving, or a Navy Corpsman, Chaplain or Religious Program Specialist who served with a Marine unit. Family adjusted gross income of $134,000 or less (2025 tax year). Not for Federal Service Academies.

scholarships.name: MOAA Education Assistance Program
scholarships.sponsor: Military Officers Association of America (MOAA) Scholarship Fund
scholarships.amount: A package of grants and/or interest-free loans; renewable up to 5 years. Extra grants for children whose parent died on active duty or receives T-SGLI.
scholarships.timing: November 1 to March 1 each year (the 2026-27 window is closed).
scholarships.rules: Students 24 or younger who are children of officers (the parent must join MOAA if selected) or of active-duty or retired enlisted members. 3.0 GPA (case-by-case exceptions), full-time undergraduate at an accredited college, 2-year program or trade school.

scholarships.name: Military Spouse and Caregiver Scholarships
scholarships.timing: Two windows a year: August 1 to September 30 and March 1 to April 30 (referrals close 3 business days before).
scholarships.rules: Spouses or caregivers of a post-9/11 service member or veteran with a combat-related injury and/or a 100% permanent and total VA rating (including Individual Unemployability); one category is for spouses of the fallen. Start with Hope For The Warriors' intake to confirm eligibility.

scholarships.name: Children of Fallen Patriots scholarships
scholarships.amount: Varies (college and trade school scholarships plus counseling)
scholarships.rules: Military children who lost a parent in the line of duty -- including combat, training accidents, service-related illness, suicide and other duty-related deaths.

scholarships.name: Freedom Alliance Scholarship Fund
scholarships.timing: Yearly; see the Freedom Alliance site.
scholarships.rules: Sons and daughters of service members who were killed or severely disabled in service. Check Freedom Alliance's scholarship site for the exact rules before applying.

scholarships.name: Edith Nourse Rogers STEM Scholarship
scholarships.amount: Up to 9 extra months (or $30,000) of benefits
scholarships.timing: Apply to VA once close to running out of benefits.
scholarships.rules: Only for people using the Post-9/11 GI Bill (veterans, service members) or the Fry Scholarship who have 6 months or less of benefits left, and are in a STEM bachelor's needing at least 120 semester credits, a covered clinical training program for healthcare professionals, or a teaching certification program.
